title: 2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final
text:
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final | image = | event = [[2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[File:Colours of Clare.svg|border|40px]] {{GG|Clare|hurling}} | team1association = | team1score = 1–20 | team2 = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|40px]] {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} | team2association = | team2score = 1–26 | details = | date = 9 June 2024 | stadium = [[Semple Stadium]] | city = [[Thurles]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Gearóid Hegarty]] (Limerick) | referee = C Lyons (Cork) | attendance = 45,148 | weather = Dry | previous = [[2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2023]] | next = [[2025 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2025]] }} The '''2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match that was played on 9 June at [[Semple Stadium]] in [[Thurles]]. It was contested by [[2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|defending]] champions [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]]. The game was televised live on [[RTÉ 2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]], alongside [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]]. The throw-in was delayed by 30 minutes due to a power cut at the stadium.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0609/1453801-munster-shc-limerick-v-clare-updates/|title=Munster SHC final recap: Limerick 1-26 Clare 1-20|date=9 June 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=10 July 2024}} Limerick, captained by [[Declan Hannon]], retained the title for a record sixth year in a row after a 1-26 to 1-20 win.{{cite web|url= https://munster.gaa.ie/event/2024-munster-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title=Limerick make it six in a row|date=9 June 2024|work=Munster GAA|accessdate=4 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-1-26-clare-1-20-as-it-happened/a1242044926.html|title=Limerick 1-26 Clare 1-20: As it happened|date=9 June 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=10 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare |date=9 June 2024|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=10 July 2024}} No team in Munster had ever won six in a row before. ==Background== The two teams were meeting in the Munster final for the third year in a row with Limerick winning the final in [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] by 1–29 to 0-29 after extra-time and also in [[2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2023]] by 1-23 to 1-22.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0605/1303110-limerick-edge-past-clare-in-munster-final-classic/|title=Limerick edge Clare in extra-time epic to win fourth Munster Championship in a row|date=7 June 2022|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=7 April 2023}} Limerick were bidding to win the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster title]] for a sixth successive year and for the 25th time overall, with Clare looking for a first Munster title since [[1998 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|1998]] and seventh title overall. This was the 64th championship game between the two counties, Limerick having 40 wins to Clare's 21 with two draws, from the previous 63. 15,000 terrace tickets were made available online on 30 May and sold out in 15 minutes.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41406023.html|title=Munster SHC final terrace tickets sell out in 15 minutes|date=30 May 2024|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=4 July 2024}} ==Match== ===Summary === {{Expand section|date=August 2024}} ===Details=== {{football box | date = 9 June 2024 | round = Final | score = 1–26 {{small|(29)}} – {{small|(23)}} 1–20 | report = https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-limerick-make-it-six-in-a-row | team1 = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|20px]] {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} | goals1 = Gearóid Hegarty 1-2; Diarmaid Byrnes (3f), Aaron Gillane (4f) 0-5 each; Tom Morrissey 0-4 (1f); Declan Hannon, Kyle Hayes, David Reidy, Shane O’Brien 0-2 each; Cathal O’Neill, Adam English 0-1 each | team2 = [[File:Colours of Clare.svg|border|20px]] {{GG|Clare|hurling}} | goals2 = Aidan McCarthy 0-8 (6f); Peter Duggan 1-1; David Fitzgerald 0-4; Tony Kelly 0-3; Mark Rodgers 0-2 (2f); Shane O’Donnell, Ian Galvin 0-1 each | stadium = [[Semple Stadium]] | referee = C Lyons (Cork)
